## Abstract

The Wallet Secure Cryptographic Application (WSCA) is the security-critical software component of the EUDI Wallet responsible for protecting and performing cryptographic operations and managing security-sensitive assets. As a core security component, a compromise of the WSCA could directly affect the security and trustworthiness of the EUDI Wallet. Under Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2981, the WSCA is therefore subject to a high level of vulnerability analysis, with AVA\_VAN.5 defined as the default assessment level.

AVA\_VAN.5 provides a rigorous analysis of potential vulnerabilities and resistance against attackers with high attack potential, providing assurance that the WSCA cannot be practically compromised through known or previously unknown vulnerabilities within the defined evaluation scope.

As the WSCA is implemented as a software-only product, its security also depends on the security properties of the underlying operating platform on which it executes. Weaknesses or vulnerabilities in the platform could undermine the security objectives of the WSCA, even where the WSCA itself is securely implemented.

Therefore, the security requirements for the underlying operating platform must be clearly defined and justified to ensure that the platform provides the necessary security properties to support the AVA\_VAN.5 vulnerability assessment level claimed for the WSCA. This document defines these requirements and establishes the security conditions that the underlying platform must satisfy so that vulnerabilities or weaknesses in the platform do not undermine the security objectives or the overall assurance level of the WSCA.

## 1 Introduction {#s-1}

### 1.1 Security problem definition {#s-1-1}

The WSCA is a software-only application running on an underlying operating system. As the WSCA is evaluated against AVA\_VAN.5, the security of the underlying platform must provide a level of protection commensurate with the security objectives and vulnerability resistance expected for the WSCA. A weakness in the underlying platform could provide an attacker with a means to bypass the security mechanisms of the WSCA and consequently undermine the AVA\_VAN.5 assurance claim.

The objective of this document is to define the security requirements and protection principles for the underlying platform on which the WSCA operates. These requirements address the platform capabilities and configuration necessary to protect the WSCA against unauthorised access, modification, interference and exploitation, and to ensure that platform vulnerabilities do not provide an attack path that would undermine the WSCA security objectives.

The WSCA and its underlying platform must be deployed in a secure and controlled operational environment. The operational environment shall provide the physical, administrative and operational controls necessary to protect the WSCA and its underlying platform against unauthorised physical access, tampering, misuse and other environmental threats. These controls include as applicable, physical protection of the servers and WSCD, controlled access to the environment, and protection of supporting infrastructure and network connections. The operational environment therefore forms an additional layer of protection and shall be sufficiently secure to ensure that the security objectives of the WSCA and the protection provided by the underlying platform are not undermined during operation.

The requirements defined in this document establish the minimum-security conditions for the underlying platform and operational environment to support the WSCA's AVA\_VAN.5 evaluation. They cover, as applicable, aspects such as minimal configuration, restricted execution, least privilege, process isolation, memory protection, controlled interfaces, platform integrity and vulnerability management.

### 1.2 Document Identification {#s-1-2}

Version: 0.7

### 1.3 Structure of the document {#s-1-3}

This document uses a step-by-step, layered approach to identify the security measures needed to protect the WSCA and support its AVA\_VAN.5 evaluation. It starts by considering the operational environment in which the WSCA is deployed, then identifies the components of the underlying platform, establishes the security principles that apply to these components, and finally translates these principles into detailed security requirements.

Section 2 — Security requirements Operational Environment: describes the conditions and security requirements that shall be in place around the WSCA and its underlying platform.

Section 3 —High-Level layered Design of the Underlying Platform: High-Level layered Design of the Underlying Platform: describes the different components that make up the underlying platform, including the hardware, bootloader, operating system kernel, system services, application space and container environment. This establishes the scope of the platform that supports the WSCA.

Section 4 — Security Principles for the Underlying Platform: defines the fundamental security principles that shall be applied to the underlying platform. These principles describe how the platform is to be protected, including minimising the attack surface, restricting execution and privileges, isolating processes, protecting memory and controlling interfaces.

Section 5 — Requirements for the Underlying Platform: translates the security principles into specific requirements for each applicable platform layer. These requirements define the security properties and configurations necessary to ensure that individual weaknesses in the underlying platform do not provide an attack path that could compromise the WSCA or undermine its AVA\_VAN.5 assurance claim.

Section 6 — Application of the Requirements for the Linux-Based Underlying Platform: This chapter describes how the defined security requirements can be implemented in a Linux-based environment.

## 2 Security requirements Operational Environment {#s-2}

This section describes the required operational environment in which the WSCA shall be deployed and identifies the architectural, platform and deployment constraints that are required to support the security objectives and assurance expectations associated with an AVA\_VAN.5 evaluation.

Section 5 defines the detailed security requirements for the dedicated underlying platform. These requirements are derived from the security principles defined in Section 4 and specify how these principles apply to the individual layers and components of the platform. The operational environment is depicted in Figure 1.

The security requirements for the operational environment in Table 1, follow the principle of minimising exposure and reducing the attack surface of the WSCA and its dedicated underlying platform and thus reduce the likelihood that a vulnerability in the operational environment or the underlying platform can be used to compromise the WSCA.

| ID                      | Security requirements Operational Environment                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|-------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| ENV- DEDICATED_PLATFROM | The WSCA operates on a dedicated underlying hardened platform and hardware that forms part of its trusted operational environment. No applications, services, workloads or processing functions unrelated to the WSCA shall be installed or operated on the hardened platforms and on top dedicated hardware. Consequently, deployment of the WSCA as a shared cloud application is not permitted. |
| ENV-TRUSTED-ADMIN | Administrators are appropriately trained, follow established policies and guidance, and are trusted to act without malicious intent. They ensure that passwords and credentials have sufficient strength and entropy. The platform enforces dual control for administrative tasks to prevent a single administrator from performing sensitive or potentially malicious actions alone.                                                                                                                                                                   |

External communication is mediated through a gateway platform positioned between the WSCA platform and the Internet. This provides an additional security boundary for network communication and reduces the direct exposure of the WSCA execution environment. The gateway implements at least DDoS protection, intrusion detection, antivirus functionality and firewall functionality.                                                                                              |

| ENV-WSCD-CHANNEL  | Communication channels between the WSCA and the WSCD and the WSCA the gateway platform shall be authenticated and encrypted. The communication mechanism shall protect the confidentiality and integrity of all exchanged security-relevant data and cryptographic commands, and shall prevent unauthorised interception, modification, replay, or impersonation of communicating parties. The communication channel between the WSCA and the WSCD shall use a dedicated physical connection, isolated from all other computer systems.                |

Access shall be restricted to authorised personnel through appropriate physical access controls. Physical security measures shall protect the WSCA, WSCD the databases and the gateway against attacks that could compromise their integrity, confidentiality, or availability, including attacks within the scope of the AVA_VAN.5 vulnerability assessment. |

## 3 High-Level layered Design of the Underlying Platform {#s-3}

The underlying platform is the complete software and hardware environment required to execute and protect the software-only WSCA. The platform consists of several layers, where each layer provides functionality and security mechanisms required by the layers above it.

For each of these layers, Section 5 defines a set of security requirements derived from the security principles described in Section 4. The High-Level layered Design is depicted in Figure 2.

Figure 2 — High-Level Design of the Underlying Platform

![Image](/img/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/nl-cs-wsca-conditions/image_000001_4da8f556a85078b2cf08ecbb9eb51956d4c69c1b86f8de792b3eb0be1792f62b.png)

### 3.1 Hardware / Host System {#s-3-1}

The hardware/host system provides the physical resources on which the underlying platform operates. This includes the processor, memory, storage, network interfaces and the physical interfaces used to connect to the WSCD. Where available, hardware-based security features such as hardware-assisted memory protection or trusted execution mechanisms may also contribute to the protection of the WSCA.

### 3.2 Boot and Initialisation Layer {#s-3-2}

The boot and initialisation layer is responsible for bringing the platform into a known and controlled state before the operating system starts. It typically includes firmware such as UEFI and a bootloader, and may include mechanisms such as Secure Boot and integrity verification. This layer is important because compromise of the boot process could allow malicious code to execute before the operating system and security controls are established.

### 3.3 Operating System Kernel {#s-3-3}

The operating system kernel provides the fundamental security and resource-management functions of the platform. It controls processes, memory, privileges, devices, system calls, inter-process communication and network functionality. The kernel is particularly securitycritical because a compromise of the kernel could allow an attacker to bypass the security controls protecting the WSCA.

### 3.4 Operating System / System Services {#s-3-4}

Operating system services provide the functionality required by the kernel and applications to operate the platform. These may include authentication and authorisation, file and storage services, cryptographic services, logging, time services, networking and system management. Only services required for the secure operation and administration of the WSCA environment should be enabled.

### 3.5 Application Space {#s-3-5}

Application space contains the software that runs above the operating system, excluding the WSCA itself. This may include supporting applications, utilities, management components and other software required to operate the platform. The application space should be minimised and controlled to reduce the possibility that vulnerabilities in unrelated applications can be used to compromise the WSCA.

### 3.6 Container / Isolation Layer {#s-3-6}

Where containers are used, the container runtime and its associated isolation mechanisms form part of the platform supporting the WSCA. Containers provide separation between applications and can restrict access to platform resources through mechanisms such as namespaces, resource controls and security policies. The security of the container runtime, container configuration and container images must therefore be considered where the WSCA executes within a container.

### 3.7 WSCA Execution Environment {#s-3-7}

The WSCA execution environment is the specific environment in which the WSCA software executes. It includes the runtime components, libraries, configuration, security policies and interfaces required by the WSCA. It also includes the interfaces through which the WSCA communicates with the WSCD and, where applicable, the gateway. The execution environment must provide the necessary isolation and protection to prevent other platform components from compromising the WSCA.

## 4 Security Principles for the Underlying Platform {#s-4}

Table 2 defines the security principles for the underlying platform. The principles are focused on reducing the attack surface, restricting execution and privileges, isolating the WSCA from other platform components, protecting its memory and security-relevant data, controlling interfaces and network exposure, and maintaining the integrity of the platform.

Table 2 — Security Principles for the Underlying Platform

|   ID | Security Principle              | Security Principal description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|------|---------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|   01 | Minimal Configuration           | The underlying platform shall be configured with only those operating system components, services, drivers, interfaces and functions that are required for the secure operation of the WSCA. Unnecessary functionality shall be disabled or removed.                  |
|   02 | Limited Execution               | The underlying platform shall restrict execution to authorised software, processes and services required for the operation of the WSCA. Execution of unauthorised software shall be prevented.                                                                        |
|   03 | Least Privilege                 | The underlying platform shall ensure that the WSCA and its supporting processes operate with only the privileges necessary to perform their specified functions.                                                                                                      |
|   04 | Process Isolation               | The underlying platform shall provide isolation between the WSCA and other processes such that an unauthorised process cannot access, modify or interfere with the WSCA or its security-relevant data.                                                                |
|   05 | Memory Protection               | The underlying platform shall protect memory allocated to the WSCA against unauthorised reading, modification and execution by other processes or users.                                                                                                              |
|   06 | Controlled Interfaces           | The underlying platform shall restrict access to system interfaces, devices, files, inter-process communication mechanisms and other resources to those required for the operation of the WSCA.                                                                       |
|   07 | Platform Integrity              | The underlying platform shall provide mechanisms to prevent or detect unauthorised modification of platform components that could affect the security of the WSCA.                                                                                                    |
|   08 | Network Protection              | The underlying platform shall expose only the network services, protocols and ports required for the operation of the WSCA. Direct network access from the WSCA to untrusted networks shall be prevented where it is not required for the WSCA's specified operation. |
|   09 | WSCA Data Protection            | The underlying platform shall protect WSCA security-relevant data, including configuration data, credentials and other sensitive information, against unauthorised disclosure, modification or deletion.                                                              |
|   10 | Privilege Escalation Protection | The underlying platform shall prevent a process or user operating with limited privileges from obtaining privileges that could be used to compromise or interfere with the WSCA.                                                                                      |
|   11 | Security-Relevant Logging       | The underlying platform shall provide logging of security-relevant events necessary to support the detection and investigation of events that could affect the security of the WSCA.                                                                                  |
|   12 | Vulnerability Management  | The underlying platform shall be maintained using a defined vulnerability and security-update management process to ensure that known vulnerabilities that could affect the WSCA are assessed and appropriately remediated.                                                                             |
|   13 | Cyber Security Monitoring | The underlying platform shall be continuously monitored for security-relevant events, anomalous behaviour, and indicators of compromise that could affect the security of the WSCA. Detected events shall be analysed and, where necessary, trigger appropriate alerts and incident response measures. |

## 5 Requirements for the Underlying Platform {#s-5}

This section defines the security requirements for each layer of the underlying platform architecture. The requirements are derived from the security principles established in Section 4 and translate these principles into concrete security objectives and controls for the individual platform layers.

Together, these requirements ensure that the underlying platform provides the security properties necessary to protect the WSCA and to support its AVA\_VAN.5 assurance objectives.

### 5.1 Hardware Requirements {#s-5-1}

The hardware/host system provides the physical foundation on which the underlying platform and WSCA operate. As the WSCA is a software-only application, compromise or manipulation of the hardware may bypass software-based security mechanisms and directly affect the confidentiality, integrity and availability of the WSCA. The hardware shall therefore be configured and operated to provide a controlled and trustworthy foundation for the platform.

| ID    | Security Principle    | Hardware Requirement                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|-------|-----------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| HW-01 | Minimal Configuration | The host system shall be configured with only the hardware components required for the operation of the WSCA platform. Unnecessary hardware devices and interfaces shall be disabled or removed where technically possible.                                                       |
| HW-02 | Limited Execution     | The hardware shall support the platform's mechanisms for restricting execution to authorised platform and WSCA software. Hardware mechanisms that could allow unauthorised code execution or bypass platform controls shall be disabled or appropriately controlled.              |
| HW-03 | Least Privilege       | Hardware resources and privileged hardware functions shall only be accessible through authorised platform mechanisms and to components requiring such access for their specified functions.                                                                                       |
| HW-04 | Process Isolation     | The host hardware shall provide, where supported, hardware-assisted mechanisms for isolating processes and execution environments, including processor privilege levels and virtual memory protection.                                                                            |
| HW-05 | Memory Protection     | The processor and memory subsystem shall support hardware-assisted memory protection mechanisms. These mechanisms shall be enabled and configured to prevent unauthorised access to memory allocated to the WSCA.                                                                 |
| HW-06 | Controlled Interfaces | Physical interfaces and peripheral devices shall be limited to those required for the operation and administration of the WSCA platform. Unnecessary interfaces, such as unused USB, storage or peripheral interfaces, shall be disabled or physically restricted where possible. |
| HW-07 | Platform Integrity    | Where supported by the hardware, mechanisms such as a hardware root of trust, Trusted Platform Module (TPM), measured boot or Secure Boot shall be used to support verification of the integrity of the platform during system initialisation.                                    |
| HW-08 | Network Protection              | Network interfaces shall be limited to those required for WSCA operation and platform administration. Unused network interfaces shall be disabled, and the hardware configuration shall not provide an uncontrolled path to untrusted networks.                                                                                                                                                     |
| HW-09 | WSCA Data Protection            | Hardware resources used to store or process WSCA security-relevant data shall be protected against unauthorised physical and logical access. Where hardware security mechanisms are available, they shall be used where required to protect sensitive data.                                                                                                                                         |
| HW-10 | Privilege Escalation Protection | The hardware shall support processor and platform security mechanisms that prevent lower-privileged software from directly accessing privileged hardware resources or bypassing the access-control mechanisms of the underlying platform.                                                                                                                                                           |
| HW-11 | Security-Relevant Logging       | Where hardware security events are relevant to the security of the WSCA, the platform shall provide mechanisms to capture or expose such events to the platform logging and monitoring functions.                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| HW-12 | Vulnerability Management        | The hardware platform, including firmware and microcode, shall be subject to a defined vulnerability-management process. Security updates addressing vulnerabilities that could affect the WSCA shall be assessed and applied in accordance with the applicable security-update policy.                                                                                                             |
| HW-13 | Cyber Security Monitoring       | The hardware platform shall support the collection and reporting of security-relevant hardware events, where technically available, including hardware faults, integrity violations, and indicators of unauthorised physical or logical access. Such events shall be made available to the platform's security monitoring mechanisms for analysis and, where necessary, trigger appropriate alerts. |

### 5.2 Boot and Initialisation Layer Requirements {#s-5-2}

The boot and initialisation layer establishes the initial state of the underlying platform before the operating system and WSCA are executed. As this layer executes before the security controls of the operating system are fully established, a compromise of the boot process could allow an attacker to introduce malicious or modified components and subsequently bypass the protection mechanisms of the platform and WSCA.

| ID      | Security Principle    | Boot and Initialisation Requirement                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
|---------|-----------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| BOOT-01 | Minimal Configuration | The boot and initialisation environment shall be configured with only the firmware, boot components and configuration required to initialise the platform and start the authorised operating system. Unnecessary boot functionality shall be disabled where technically possible. |
| BOOT-02 | Limited Execution     | The boot process shall permit execution only of authorised firmware, bootloader components and operating system components. Unauthorised code shall not be permitted to execute during platform initialisation.                                                                   |
| BOOT-03 | Least Privilege       | Boot and initialisation components shall operate with only the privileges and access to hardware resources necessary to perform platform initialisation and start the authorised operating system.                                                                                |
| BOOT-04 | Process Isolation     | The boot environment shall prevent unauthorised or untrusted components from gaining access to or interfering with security-relevant boot processes and initialisation components.                                                                                                |
| BOOT-05 | Memory Protection               | The boot environment shall use available hardware and firmware mechanisms to protect memory used during initialisation against unauthorised access or modification.                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| BOOT-06 | Controlled Interfaces           | Access to firmware configuration, boot interfaces and hardware configuration functions shall be restricted to authorised personnel or authorised management mechanisms. Unnecessary boot interfaces shall be disabled or otherwise restricted.                                                                                                         |
| BOOT-07 | Platform Integrity              | The boot process shall provide mechanisms to verify the authenticity and/or integrity of firmware, bootloader and operating system components before they are executed. Where supported, Secure Boot, measured boot or equivalent integrity mechanisms shall be enabled and appropriately configured.                                                  |
| BOOT-08 | Network Protection              | Network functionality during the boot and initialisation process shall be disabled unless required for a defined platform function. Where network boot or other pre-OS network functionality is required, it shall be restricted to authorised sources and protected against unauthorised modification or execution.                                   |
| BOOT-09 | WSCA Data Protection            | The boot and initialisation process shall not expose or provide unauthorised access to WSCA security-relevant data stored on the platform. Access to storage containing WSCA data during boot shall be restricted to authorised platform components.                                                                                                   |
| BOOT-10 | Privilege Escalation Protection | The boot and initialisation mechanisms shall prevent lower-trust or unauthorised components from obtaining privileged execution through manipulation of the boot process, boot configuration or firmware interfaces.                                                                                                                                   |
| BOOT-11 | Security-Relevant Logging       | Where supported, security-relevant boot and integrity events, including failed integrity checks and unauthorised boot attempts, shall be recorded and made available to the platform's security monitoring mechanisms.                                                                                                                                 |
| BOOT-12 | Vulnerability Management        | Firmware, bootloader and other boot components shall be subject to a defined vulnerability-management process. Security vulnerabilities affecting the integrity or security of the WSCA platform shall be assessed and appropriately remediated.                                                                                                       |
| BOOT-13 | Cyber Security Monitoring       | The boot and initialisation process shall support the detection of security-relevant anomalies, including unexpected boot configurations, failed integrity verification, and unauthorised changes to boot components. Detected events shall be reported to the platform's security monitoring mechanisms to enable timely investigation and response. |

### 5.3 Operating System Kernel Requirements {#s-5-3}

The operating system kernel provides the fundamental security and resource-management functions on which the WSCA relies. It controls processes, memory, privileges, devices, system calls and inter-process communication. A compromise of the kernel could allow an attacker to bypass the security mechanisms protecting the WSCA. The kernel shall therefore be configured and operated to provide strong isolation, access control and protection of the WSCA execution environment.

| ID      | Security Principle    | Operating System Kernel Requirement                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
|---------|-----------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| KERN-01 | Minimal Configuration | The kernel shall be configured with only the functionality, drivers, modules and interfaces required for the secure operation of the WSCA platform. Unnecessary kernel functionality shall be disabled or removed where technically possible. |
| KERN-02 | Limited Execution               | The kernel shall prevent unauthorised kernel modules, drivers or other privileged code from being loaded or executed. Only authorised and trusted kernel components shall be permitted.                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| KERN-03 | Least Privilege                 | The kernel shall provide mechanisms to enforce separation between privileged and non-privileged execution and shall ensure that the WSCA operates with only the privileges required for its specified functions.                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| KERN-04 | Process Isolation               | The kernel shall provide process isolation mechanisms that prevent one process from accessing, modifying or interfering with another process unless explicitly authorised.                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| KERN-05 | Memory Protection               | The kernel shall enforce memory isolation and shall prevent unauthorised processes from reading, modifying or executing memory allocated to the WSCA. Hardware-assisted memory protection mechanisms shall be enabled where available.                                                                                                                                                           |
| KERN-06 | Controlled Interfaces           | Access to kernel interfaces, system calls, devices, IPC mechanisms and other kernel-managed resources shall be restricted according to the privileges and functions of the requesting process.                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| KERN-07 | Platform Integrity              | The kernel shall provide mechanisms to protect the integrity of its own code, security configuration and security-relevant data during operation.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| KERN-08 | Network Protection              | The kernel network stack shall be configured to expose only the network functionality required by the WSCA environment. Unnecessary network protocols, interfaces and services shall be disabled.                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| KERN-09 | WSCA Data Protection            | The kernel shall enforce access controls preventing unauthorised processes or users from accessing WSCA security-relevant files, memory, devices and other resources.                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| KERN-10 | Privilege Escalation Protection | The kernel shall provide mechanisms to prevent processes operating with limited privileges from obtaining unauthorised higher privileges or bypassing kernel access-control mechanisms.                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| KERN-11 | Security-Relevant Logging       | The kernel shall provide logging or security event mechanisms for security-relevant events that could indicate an attempt to bypass kernel security controls or compromise the WSCA.                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| KERN-12 | Vulnerability Management        | The kernel and its security-relevant modules and drivers shall be subject to vulnerability management. Known vulnerabilities that could affect the WSCA shall be assessed and appropriately remediated.                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| KERN-13 | Cyber Security Monitoring       | The operating system kernel shall support the detection and reporting of security-relevant anomalies, including unauthorised privilege escalation, unexpected kernel module loading, violations of access controls, and attempts to exploit kernel vulnerabilities. Detected events shall be made available to the platform's security monitoring mechanisms for analysis and incident response. |

### 5.4 Operating System / System Services Requirements {#s-5-4}

Operating system services provide functionality used by the WSCA and other components of the platform. Because vulnerabilities in unnecessary or improperly configured services can provide attack paths to the WSCA, only required services shall be enabled and their access shall be appropriately restricted.

| ID    | Security Principle              | Operating System / System Services Requirement                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
|-------|---------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| OS-01 | Minimal Configuration           | Only operating system services required for the secure operation, administration and maintenance of the WSCA shall be installed and enabled.                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| OS-02 | Limited Execution               | System services shall execute only authorised binaries and components. Unauthorised modification or replacement of service executables shall be prevented or detected.                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| OS-03 | Least Privilege                 | Each system service required by the WSCA shall operate using the minimum privileges and system resources necessary for its function.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| OS-04 | Process Isolation               | System services shall be isolated from the WSCA and from each other to the extent necessary to prevent compromise of one service from directly compromising the WSCA.                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| OS-05 | Memory Protection               | System services shall operate using the platform's available memory protection mechanisms so that they cannot access or modify WSCA memory without authorisation.                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| OS-06 | Controlled Interfaces           | Access to system services shall be restricted to authorised users, processes and network endpoints. Unused service interfaces shall be disabled.                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| OS-07 | Platform Integrity              | System service configuration and security policies shall be protected against unauthorised modification.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| OS-08 | Network Protection              | Network-facing services shall be limited to those required by the WSCA environment. Services that are not required shall be disabled and their associated ports shall not be exposed.                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| OS-09 | WSCA Data Protection            | System services shall not provide unauthorised access to WSCA files, configuration, credentials or other security-relevant data.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| OS-10 | Privilege Escalation Protection | System services shall be configured to prevent their interfaces or vulnerabilities from being used to obtain privileges that could compromise the WSCA.                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| OS-11 | Security-Relevant Logging       | Security-relevant events generated by system services shall be logged where required to detect or investigate activity that could affect WSCA security.                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| OS-12 | Vulnerability Management        | System services and associated components shall be regularly assessed for vulnerabilities and security updates shall be applied where required.                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| OS-13 | Cyber Security Monitoring       | The operating system shall continuously monitor system services for security-relevant anomalies, including unexpected service behaviour, unauthorised configuration changes, suspicious process activity, and indicators of compromise. Detected events shall be reported to the platform's security monitoring mechanisms for analysis, alerting, and incident response. |

### 5.5 Application Space Requirements {#s-5-5}

The application space contains software running above the operating system, excluding the WSCA itself. Unnecessary applications and utilities increase the attack surface and may provide an attacker with an indirect path towards the WSCA. The application space shall therefore be strictly controlled.

| ID     | Security Principle    | Application Space Requirement                                                                                                          |
|--------|-----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| APP-01 | Minimal Configuration | Only applications and utilities required for the operation, administration and maintenance of the WSCA environment shall be installed. |
| APP-02 | Limited Execution               | Execution of applications, scripts and utilities shall be restricted to authorised software. Application allow-listing or equivalent controls shall be applied where technically feasible.                                                                                                                                                                 |
| APP-03 | Least Privilege                 | Applications and utilities shall operate with the minimum privileges required for their intended functions.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| APP-04 | Process Isolation               | Applications shall be isolated from the WSCA so that compromise of an application does not provide direct access to WSCA processes or resources.                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| APP-05 | Memory Protection               | Applications shall not be able to read, modify or execute WSCA memory unless explicitly authorised and required for operation.                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| APP-06 | Controlled Interfaces           | Applications shall have access only to the system interfaces, files, devices and services required for their intended functions.                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| APP-07 | Platform Integrity              | Application binaries and security-relevant configuration shall be protected against unauthorised modification.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| APP-08 | Network Protection              | Applications shall not establish network connections to untrusted networks unless explicitly required and authorised.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| APP-09 | WSCA Data Protection            | Applications shall be prevented from accessing WSCA security-relevant data unless explicitly authorised.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| APP-10 | Privilege Escalation Protection | Applications shall be configured and controlled to prevent exploitation of application vulnerabilities from resulting in unauthorised privilege escalation affecting the WSCA.                                                                                                                                                                             |
| APP-11 | Security-Relevant Logging       | Security-relevant application events that could indicate an attempt to compromise the WSCA environment shall be logged where appropriate.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| APP-12 | Vulnerability Management        | Applications installed on the platform shall be subject to vulnerability management. Unnecessary or unsupported applications shall be removed.                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| APP-13 | Cyber Security Monitoring       | Applications in the WSCA environment shall be monitored for security-relevant anomalies, including unauthorised execution, unexpected application behaviour, suspicious process activity, and indicators of compromise. Detected events shall be reported to the platform's security monitoring mechanisms for analysis, alerting, and incident response. |

### 5.6 Container / Isolation Layer Requirements {#s-5-6}

Where the WSCA is deployed within a container, the container runtime and associated isolation mechanisms form part of the underlying platform. The container layer shall prevent the WSCA from being exposed to unnecessary host resources or to other containers and shall ensure that a compromise of a container does not provide an uncontrolled path to the host or WSCA environment.

| ID      | Security Principle    | Container / Isolation Layer Requirement                                                                                                             |
|---------|-----------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| CONT-01 | Minimal Configuration | Container images shall contain only the software, libraries and configuration required for the intended WSCA function.                              |
| CONT-02 | Limited Execution     | Only authorised container images and workloads shall be permitted to execute. Container images shall originate from controlled and trusted sources. |
| CONT-03 | Least Privilege       | Containers shall execute with the minimum privileges required. Privileged containers shall not be used unless explicitly justified and authorised.  |
| CONT-04 | Process Isolation               | Containers shall be isolated from the host, other containers and unrelated processes using the platform's available isolation mechanisms.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| CONT-05 | Memory Protection               | Container resource controls shall prevent one container from accessing or exhausting memory resources in a manner that could compromise the WSCA or the underlying platform.                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| CONT-06 | Controlled Interfaces           | Container access to host devices, filesystems, kernel interfaces and other host resources shall be explicitly restricted. Unnecessary host mounts and device access shall not be permitted.                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| CONT-07 | Platform Integrity              | Container images, runtime components and container configuration shall be integrity-protected and changes shall be controlled.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| CONT-08 | Network Protection              | Container network connectivity shall be restricted to the connections required for WSCA operation. Unnecessary external network access shall be prevented.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| CONT-09 | WSCA Data Protection            | Containers shall not have access to WSCA security-relevant data unless such access is explicitly required for the WSCA function.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| CONT-10 | Privilege Escalation Protection | Container configuration and runtime controls shall prevent container processes from escaping their isolation boundary or obtaining unauthorised host privileges.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| CONT-11 | Security-Relevant Logging       | Container runtime and security events relevant to the protection of the WSCA shall be logged and made available for monitoring where appropriate.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| CONT-12 | Vulnerability Management        | Container images, runtimes and supporting components shall be regularly assessed for vulnerabilities. Vulnerable or unsupported images and components shall be updated or removed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| CONT-13 | Cyber Security Monitoring       | The container runtime and isolation mechanisms shall be monitored for security-relevant anomalies, including unauthorised container creation or modification, attempted isolation-boundary violations, unexpected resource access, and suspicious workload behaviour. Detected events shall be reported to the platform's security monitoring mechanisms for analysis, alerting, and incident response. |

### 5.7 WSCA Execution Environment Requirements {#s-5-7}

The WSCA execution environment is the final platform layer immediately supporting the WSCA software. This layer includes the runtime components, libraries, configuration and security policies on which the WSCA directly depends. Particular care shall be taken to ensure that the WSCA has access only to the resources required for its security functions.

| ID      | Security Principle             | WSCA Execution Environment Requirement                                                                                                         |
|---------|--------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| WSCA-01 | Minimal Configuration The by   | WSCA execution environment shall contain only the runtime components, libraries, configuration and supporting functionality required the WSCA. |
|         | Limited Execution Only be      | WSCA-02 authorised WSCA binaries, libraries and supporting components shall permitted to execute within the WSCA execution environment.        |
|         | Least Privilege The privileges | WSCA-03 WSCA shall execute with the minimum operating system and platform required to perform its specified security functions.                |
| WSCA-04 | Process Isolation               | The WSCA shall be isolated from unrelated applications, services and processes such that compromise of another component does not provide direct access to the WSCA.                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| WSCA-05 | Memory Protection               | The WSCA execution environment shall enforce memory protection mechanisms preventing unauthorised access to WSCA memory and security-relevant runtime data.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| WSCA-06 | Controlled Interfaces           | The WSCA shall have access only to the platform interfaces, devices, files and services required for its specified operation.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| WSCA-07 | Platform Integrity              | WSCA binaries, libraries and security-relevant configuration shall be protected against unauthorised modification.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| WSCA-08 | Network Protection              | Network communication from the WSCA shall be restricted to explicitly authorised endpoints and protocols required for its operation.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| WSCA-09 | WSCA Data Protection            | Security-relevant WSCA data shall be protected against unauthorised disclosure, modification and deletion by the underlying platform and other processes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| WSCA-10 | Privilege Escalation Protection | The execution environment shall prevent the WSCA or its supporting components from obtaining privileges beyond those required for their specified functions.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| WSCA-11 | Security-Relevant Logging       | Security-relevant events affecting the WSCA execution environment shall be logged where necessary to support detection and investigation of security events.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| WSCA-12 | Vulnerability Management        | All runtime components, libraries and supporting software on which the WSCA depends shall be subject to vulnerability management and security-update processes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| WSCA-13 | Cyber Security Monitoring       | The WSCA execution environment shall be continuously monitored for security-relevant anomalies, including unauthorised changes to runtime components or configuration, unexpected WSCA behaviour, suspicious resource access, and indicators of compromise. Detected events shall be reported to the platform's security monitoring mechanisms for analysis, alerting, and incident response. |

## 6 Application of the Requirements for the Linux-Based Underlying Platform {#s-6}

This chapter describes how the defined security requirements can be implemented in a Linux-based environment. Section 6.1 identifies the relevant Linux security mechanisms that may be used to fulfil the requirements. The subsequent sections describe, for each requirement, how the applicable mechanisms can be applied and configured to provide the required security properties.

Not all mechanisms must be used. The developer shall select an appropriate combination of mechanisms based on the platform architecture. The selected mechanisms shall be properly justified as providing the required security properties; equivalent mechanisms may be used where appropriate.

### 6.1 Linux and Hardware Security Mechanisms Mapping {#s-6-1}

Table 3 identifies the Linux and hardware security mechanisms that can be used to implement the security principles and requirements defined for the underlying platform. It provides a technical link between the required security properties and their implementation in a Linux-based environment.

Table 3 — Linux and Hardware security mechanisms

| Security Mechanism                   | Primary security purpose                                                                                                  | Relevant platform layer   |
|--------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------|
| UEFI Secure Boot                     | Establishes an authenticated chain of trust from firmware to bootloader and operating system.                             | Hardware / Boot           |
| TPM 2.0                              | Provides hardware-backed protection for keys and platform integrity measurements                                          | Hardware / Boot           |
| TPM measured boot                    | Records measurements of firmware, bootloader, kernel and other boot components to support platform integrity verification | Boot                      |
| UEFI firmware controls               | Restricts hardware configuration, boot sources and pre-OS interfaces                                                      | Hardware / Boot           |
| GRUB bootloader protection           | Protects kernel selection, boot parameters and recovery functions against unauthorised modification                       | Boot                      |
| Signed Linux kernel / kernel modules | Prevents execution of unauthorised or modified privileged code                                                            | Boot / Kernel             |
| Linux MMU / virtual memory           | Provides memory isolation between processes and between user and kernel space                                             | Hardware / Kernel         |
| CPU privilege levels                 | Separates privileged kernel execution from unprivileged user-space execution                                             | Hardware / Kernel         |
| NX/XD                                | Prevents execution of code from memory regions designated as non-executable                                               | Hardware / Kernel         |
| ASLR                                 | Randomises memory locations to make exploitation of memory-corruption vulnerabilities more difficult                      | Kernel / WSCA             |
| SMEP                             | Prevents the kernel from executing code located in user-space memory                          | Hardware / Kernel                                    |
| SMAP                             | Prevents unintended kernel access to user-space memory                                        | Hardware / Kernel                                    |
| IOMMU                            | Restricts DMA-capable devices from accessing unauthorised memory regions                      | Hardware / Kernel                                    |
| Hardware-assisted virtualisation | Provides hardware support for isolation between virtual machines or execution environments    | Hardware / Isolation                                 |
| Linux users and groups           | Provides identity-based separation and basic access control                                   | Kernel / Services / Applications                     |
| Linux filesystem permissions     | Restricts read, write and execute access to files and directories                             | Kernel / Services / Applications / WSCA              |
| Linux capabilities               | Splits root privileges into individually controllable privileges and supports least privilege | Kernel / Services / Containers / WSCA                |
| SELinux                          | Provides mandatory access control and confinement of processes and resources                  | Kernel / Services / Applications / Containers / WSCA |
| AppArmor                         | Provides mandatory application access-control and confinement policies                        | Kernel / Services / Applications / Containers / WSCA |
| seccomp                          | Restricts the system calls available to a process and reduces its kernel attack surface       | Kernel / Applications / Containers / WSCA            |
| Linux namespaces                 | Isolates processes and resources between execution environments                               | Kernel / Containers / WSCA                           |
| PID namespaces                   | Isolates process visibility and process identifiers                                           | Containers / Isolation                               |
| User namespaces                  | Isolates user and group identities and allows restricted container root identities            | Containers / Isolation                               |
| Mount namespaces                 | Isolates filesystem mount points and restricts visibility of host filesystems                 | Containers / Isolation / WSCA                        |
| Network namespaces               | Isolates network interfaces, routes and network stacks                                        | Containers / Isolation                               |
| IPC namespaces                   | Isolates inter-process communication resources                                                | Containers / Isolation                               |
| cgroups                          | Controls and limits CPU, memory and other resource consumption                                | Kernel / Containers / Services                       |
| systemd service isolation        | Restricts service privileges, resources, filesystem access and available system functionality | System Services / WSCA                               |
| systemd NoNewPrivileges          | Prevents a process and its children from acquiring additional privileges                      | Services / WSCA                                      |
| systemd filesystem restrictions  | Restricts service access to host filesystems and sensitive directories                        | Services / WSCA                                      |
| systemd device restrictions      | Restricts access to hardware devices exposed through /dev                                     | Services / WSCA                                      |
| systemd namespace isolation      | Creates additional isolation boundaries for system services                                   | Services / WSCA                                      |
| Container runtime                              | Enforces and manages container isolation using Linux kernel security mechanisms                                                                         | Container / Isolation                   |
| Container image signing / verification         | Ensures that only authorised and trusted container images are deployed                                                                                  | Container / Isolation                   |
| Container capability restrictions              | Removes unnecessary Linux privileges from container processes                                                                                           | Container / Isolation                   |
| Container device controls                      | Prevents unnecessary access to host hardware devices                                                                                                    | Container / Isolation                   |
| Filesystem / volume controls                   | Restricts container and WSCA access to persistent data                                                                                                  | Containers / WSCA                       |
| nftables                                       | Restricts network connections, ports, protocols and communication paths                                                                                 | Kernel / Services / Applications / WSCA |
| Linux routing controls                         | Controls permitted network paths and prevents unintended network connectivity                                                                           | Kernel / Network                        |
| LUKS2 / dm-crypt                               | Protects stored data against unauthorised access when storage is not otherwise protected                                                                | Hardware / Storage                      |
| auditd / Linux Audit                           | Records security-relevant system calls, authentication, privilege and policy events                                                                     | Kernel / Services / Applications        |
| systemd-journald                               | Collects and manages system and service security-relevant events                                                                                        | Services / Applications / WSCA          |
| File integrity monitoring                      | Detects unauthorised modification of executables, libraries and configuration                                                                           | Services / Applications / WSCA          |
| Kernel hardening configuration                 | Reduces exploitable kernel functionality and strengthens kernel security boundaries                                                                     | Kernel                                  |
| Kernel module restrictions                     | Prevents unauthorised kernel extensions from introducing privileged code                                                                                | Kernel                                  |
| Device access controls                         | Restricts processes from directly accessing hardware devices                                                                                            | Kernel / Containers / WSCA              |
| Package management and security updates        | Maintains platform components against known vulnerabilities                                                                                             | All software layers                     |
| Vulnerability scanning / dependency management | Identifies known vulnerabilities in Linux packages, libraries, containers and dependencies                                                              | All software layers                     |
| Security monitoring / SIEM integration         | Collects and correlates security events from logs, audit facilities, integrity monitoring and runtime sensors; supports alerting and incident response. | All layers                              |

### 6.2 Hardware / Host System for Linux {#s-6-2}

The hardware layer provides security mechanisms that are either directly enforced by the processor and firmware or exposed to and controlled by Linux. Relevant mechanisms include CPU privilege levels, the Memory Management Unit (MMU), NX/XD, SMEP, SMAP, IOMMU, hardware random-number generation, TPM 2.0, Secure Boot, measured boot, hardwareassisted virtualisation and hardware device controls.

The Linux kernel uses these mechanisms to establish separation between kernel and user space, protect process memory and control access to hardware resources. Where supported, a TPM can provide a hardware root of trust for platform integrity measurements and protected key operations.

| ID    | Security Principle              | Requirement Implementation for Linux                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|-------|---------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| HW-01 | Minimal Configuration           | Only hardware required for the WSCA platform shall be present or enabled. Unused devices and interfaces shall be disabled in firmware and shall not be exposed to Linux.                                                                                                                                |
| HW-02 | Limited Execution               | Processor execution-control mechanisms such as NX/XD, SMEP and SMAP shall be enabled where supported. These shall prevent execution or inappropriate access to memory in ways that could bypass Linux security controls.                                                                                |
| HW-03 | Least Privilege                 | Direct hardware access shall be mediated by the Linux kernel. User-space processes shall not have direct access to privileged hardware resources unless explicitly required.                                                                                                                            |
| HW-04 | Process Isolation               | The processor's privilege levels and MMU shall be used to maintain separation between kernel space and user space and between individual processes.                                                                                                                                                     |
| HW-05 | Memory Protection               | Hardware memory protection shall be enabled and used by Linux to prevent one process from accessing another process's memory.                                                                                                                                                                           |
| HW-06 | Controlled Interfaces           | Unused physical interfaces such as USB, Bluetooth and wireless interfaces shall be disabled or physically restricted. Unauthorised boot devices shall be prevented.                                                                                                                                     |
| HW-07 | Platform Integrity              | Secure Boot and TPM-based measured boot shall be used where supported to establish and verify the integrity of the Linux boot chain.                                                                                                                                                                    |
| HW-08 | Network Protection              | Only required physical network interfaces shall be enabled. Unused interfaces shall be disabled at firmware or Linux level.                                                                                                                                                                             |
| HW-09 | WSCA Data Protection            | Storage containing WSCA security-relevant data shall be physically protected. Linux disk encryption, such as LUKS2, shall be used where protection of data at rest is required.                                                                                                                         |
| HW-10 | Privilege Escalation Protection | Hardware privilege separation, NX/XD, SMEP, SMAP and other available processor protections shall be enabled to prevent user-space software from bypassing kernel protection.                                                                                                                            |
| HW-11 | Security-Relevant Logging       | Relevant hardware and firmware security events exposed to Linux shall be collected through the system logging or auditing mechanisms.                                                                                                                                                                   |
| HW-12 | Vulnerability Management        | Firmware, microcode, hardware drivers and other hardware-dependent components shall be included in the platform vulnerability-management process.                                                                                                                                                       |
| HW-13 | Cyber Security Monitoring       | Where supported, hardware and firmware security events—including integrity failures, hardware faults and indicators of unauthorised physical or logical access—shall be exposed to platform monitoring mechanisms. Events shall be analysed and, where warranted, trigger alerts and incident response. |

### 6.3 Boot and Initialisation for Linux {#s-6-3}
