A Linux-based platform normally uses UEFI firmware, UEFI Secure Boot, a bootloader such as GRUB, a signed Linux kernel, initramfs/early userspace and optionally TPM-based measured boot.

Secure Boot establishes a chain of authenticated executable components. Measured boot can record measurements of firmware, bootloader, kernel and other components in the TPM. Linux can subsequently use these measurements for platform integrity verification or attestation.

| ID      | Security Principle              | Requirement Implementation for Linux                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
|---------|---------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| BOOT-01 | Minimal Configuration           | UEFI, GRUB and initramfs shall contain only components required to start the approved Linux system. Unnecessary boot functionality shall be disabled.                                                                                                                                                                           |
| BOOT-02 | Limited Execution               | UEFI Secure Boot shall be enabled where supported. Only authorised firmware, bootloader and kernel components shall be executed.                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| BOOT-03 | Least Privilege                 | Access to firmware configuration and boot configuration shall be restricted to authorised administrators.                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| BOOT-04 | Process Isolation               | The boot chain shall execute only trusted components and shall prevent unauthorised components from being introduced into the initialisation process.                                                                                                                                                                           |
| BOOT-05 | Memory Protection               | Hardware memory-protection mechanisms shall be active during boot and shall be inherited by the Linux kernel.                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| BOOT-06 | Controlled Interfaces           | UEFI configuration, GRUB configuration and recovery/single-user boot functions shall be protected against unauthorised use.                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| BOOT-07 | Platform Integrity              | Secure Boot shall verify the authenticity/integrity of boot components. TPM measured boot shall be used where appropriate to provide additional integrity evidence.                                                                                                                                                             |
| BOOT-08 | Network Protection              | PXE and other pre-OS network functionality shall be disabled unless explicitly required.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| BOOT-09 | WSCA Data Protection            | The boot environment shall not expose WSCA security-relevant data or cryptographic material to unauthorised users or components.                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| BOOT-10 | Privilege Escalation Protection | GRUB command-line access, kernel parameters and recovery modes shall be protected against unauthorised modification or use.                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| BOOT-11 | Security-Relevant Logging       | Boot integrity failures and relevant boot security events shall be recorded where supported.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| BOOT-12 | Vulnerability Management        | UEFI, GRUB, kernel, initramfs and associated boot components shall be included in vulnerability management and security updates.                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| BOOT-13 | Cyber Security Monitoring       | The boot and initialisation process shall support detection and reporting of security-relevant anomalies, including unexpected boot configurations, failed integrity verification and unauthorised changes to boot components. Events shall be made available to platform monitoring mechanisms for investigation and response. |

### 6.4 Operating System Kernel for Linux {#s-6-4}

The Linux kernel provides the most important security mechanisms for protecting the WSCA. These include process isolation, virtual memory protection, Linux capabilities, namespaces, seccomp, SELinux/AppArmor, kernel module controls, filesystem permissions, device access controls, kernel hardening mechanisms, network controls and audit facilities.

Linux also provides security mechanisms such as ASLR, NX, kernel address-space protection, read-only kernel memory protections, module signing and restrictions on privileged operations.

These mechanisms form the principal platform security boundary between the WSCA and other software executing on the host.

| ID      | Security Principle              | Requirement Implementation for Linux                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|---------|---------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| KERN-01 | Minimal Configuration           | The Linux kernel shall contain only required drivers, filesystems, protocols and functionality. Unnecessary kernel modules shall be removed or disabled.                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| KERN-02 | Limited Execution               | Kernel module loading and privileged kernel extensions shall be restricted. Module signing shall be enabled where supported, and unauthorised modules shall not be loaded.                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| KERN-03 | Least Privilege                 | The WSCA shall execute as a dedicated non-root user wherever possible. Linux capabilities shall be used instead of unrestricted root privileges.                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| KERN-04 | Process Isolation               | Linux process isolation shall be enforced through normal process separation and, where appropriate, namespaces and SELinux/AppArmor.                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| KERN-05 | Memory Protection               | ASLR, NX/XD, SMEP, SMAP and other available kernel memory protections shall be enabled. Processes shall not be able to access WSCA memory belonging to another process.                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| KERN-06 | Controlled Interfaces           | Access to system calls, /proc, /sys, devices, IPC and other kernel interfaces shall be restricted. seccomp shall be used where appropriate to reduce the WSCA system-call attack surface.                                                                                                                                                                     |
| KERN-07 | Platform Integrity              | Kernel configuration, modules and security settings shall be protected against unauthorised modification.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| KERN-08 | Network Protection              | Linux networking shall expose only required interfaces, protocols and ports. nftables or equivalent firewall controls shall restrict network communication.                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| KERN-09 | WSCA Data Protection            | Linux permissions, capabilities and SELinux/AppArmor policies shall prevent unrelated processes from accessing WSCA files, devices and other protected resources.                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| KERN-10 | Privilege Escalation Protection | Linux capabilities, SELinux/AppArmor, seccomp and kernel hardening mechanisms shall be used to reduce the possibility of privilege escalation.                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| KERN-11 | Security-Relevant Logging       | auditd, journald and kernel audit facilities shall record relevant security events.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| KERN-12 | Vulnerability Management        | The Linux kernel and security-relevant modules and drivers shall be maintained using a controlled security-update process.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| KERN-13 | Cyber Security Monitoring       | The operating system kernel shall support detection and reporting of security-relevant anomalies, including unexpected kernel-module loading, access-control violations, suspicious privileged activity and indicators of attempted kernel exploitation. Events shall be made available to platform monitoring mechanisms for analysis and incident response. |

### 6.5 Operating System / System Services for Linux {#s-6-5}

Linux system services are commonly managed through systemd. Security mechanisms include systemd service isolation and sandboxing, Linux users and groups, capabilities, SELinux/AppArmor, filesystem permissions, network namespaces, cgroups, firewall controls and audit/logging facilities.

Systemd provides additional controls such as NoNewPrivileges, filesystem restrictions, device restrictions, private temporary directories and namespace-based isolation.

| ID    | Security Principle              | Requirement Implementation for Linux                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|-------|---------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| OS-01 | Minimal Configuration           | Only system services required for WSCA operation, administration or security monitoring shall be installed and enabled.                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| OS-02 | Limited Execution               | Systemd shall start only authorised services and binaries. Service executables shall be protected against modification.                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| OS-03 | Least Privilege                 | Services shall run under dedicated non-root accounts. Linux capabilities and systemd NoNewPrivileges shall be used where applicable.                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| OS-04 | Process Isolation               | Services shall be isolated using SELinux/AppArmor and systemd sandboxing where appropriate.                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| OS-05 | Memory Protection               | Normal Linux process memory isolation shall prevent services from accessing WSCA memory.                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| OS-06 | Controlled Interfaces           | Service sockets, files, devices and IPC interfaces shall be restricted using Linux permissions and mandatory access controls.                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| OS-07 | Platform Integrity              | Service binaries and configuration files shall be writable only by authorised administrative processes.                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| OS-08 | Network Protection              | Only required network services shall listen on the host. nftables shall restrict access to permitted sources and destinations.                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| OS-09 | WSCA Data Protection            | Services shall have no access to WSCA security-relevant data unless explicitly required. SELinux/AppArmor shall enforce this where appropriate.                                                                                                                                                                      |
| OS-10 | Privilege Escalation Protection | Services shall use restricted capabilities, NoNewPrivileges and appropriate sandboxing to prevent privilege escalation.                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| OS-11 | Security-Relevant Logging       | Systemd/journald and audit facilities shall record security-relevant service events.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| OS-12 | Vulnerability Management        | Installed system services and packages shall be regularly updated and unsupported services shall be removed.                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| OS-13 | Cyber Security Monitoring       | System services shall be monitored for security-relevant anomalies, including unexpected behaviour, unauthorised configuration changes, suspicious process activity and indicators of compromise. Detected events shall be forwarded to platform monitoring mechanisms for analysis, alerting and incident response. |

### 6.6 Application Space for Linux {#s-6-6}

Linux provides several mechanisms to control application software, including Unix users/groups, filesystem permissions, Linux capabilities, SELinux/AppArmor, seccomp, systemd sandboxing, namespaces, cgroups and executable/file integrity controls.

The key objective at this layer is to ensure that an unrelated application cannot become an attack path towards the WSCA.

| ID     | Security Principle              | Requirement Implementation for Linux                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|--------|---------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| APP-01 | Minimal Configuration           | Only software required for WSCA operation and authorised administration shall be installed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| APP-02 | Limited Execution               | Execution shall be restricted to authorised applications. SELinux/AppArmor and appropriate filesystem permissions shall prevent unauthorised execution or modification.                                                                                                                                                                    |
| APP-03 | Least Privilege                 | Applications shall use dedicated users and shall not execute with root privileges unless explicitly justified.                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| APP-04 | Process Isolation               | Applications shall be isolated from the WSCA using Linux process isolation, SELinux/AppArmor and, where appropriate, namespaces.                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| APP-05 | Memory Protection               | Linux process memory isolation shall prevent applications from reading or modifying WSCA memory.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| APP-06 | Controlled Interfaces           | Access to files, devices, sockets, /proc, /sys and other system interfaces shall be restricted.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| APP-07 | Platform Integrity              | Application binaries, libraries and configuration shall be protected against unauthorised modification.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| APP-08 | Network Protection              | Applications shall have no unrestricted network access. Linux firewall rules shall restrict network communication.                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| APP-09 | WSCA Data Protection            | SELinux/AppArmor and filesystem permissions shall prevent applications from accessing WSCA data unless explicitly authorised.                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| APP-10 | Privilege Escalation Protection | Applications shall operate without unnecessary capabilities. seccomp and mandatory access controls shall be used where appropriate.                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| APP-11 | Security-Relevant Logging       | Security-relevant application events shall be recorded through journald, auditd or equivalent mechanisms.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| APP-12 | Vulnerability Management        | Application packages and dependencies shall be maintained and vulnerable or unsupported applications shall be removed or updated.                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| APP-13 | Cyber Security Monitoring       | Applications in the WSCA environment shall be monitored for security-relevant anomalies, including unauthorised execution, unexpected application behaviour, suspicious process activity and indicators of compromise. Detected events shall be forwarded to platform monitoring mechanisms for analysis, alerting and incident response. |

### 6.7 Container / Isolation Layer for Linux {#s-6-7}

Linux provides the fundamental mechanisms used by modern container technologies. These include namespaces, cgroups, Linux capabilities, seccomp, SELinux/AppArmor, filesystem namespaces, device cgroups and Linux network isolation.

The container runtime, such as containerd, Podman or Docker, combines these kernel mechanisms to create an isolated execution environment.

For an AVA\_VAN.5 evaluation, the container boundary should therefore not be treated as an independent security mechanism. Its security depends substantially on the correct configuration of the Linux kernel and container runtime.

| ID      | Security Principle    | Requirement Implementation for Linux                                                            |
|---------|-----------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| CONT-01 | Minimal Configuration | Container images shall use a minimal base image and contain only software required by the WSCA. |
| CONT-02 | Limited Execution               | Only authorised and integrity-verified container images shall be executed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| CONT-03 | Least Privilege                 | Containers shall run as non-root users where possible. Unnecessary Linux capabilities shall be dropped.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| CONT-04 | Process Isolation               | PID, user, mount, network and IPC namespaces shall isolate the WSCA container from the host and other containers.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| CONT-05 | Memory Protection               | cgroups shall limit container resource consumption. Container processes shall not be able to access host or other-container memory.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| CONT-06 | Controlled Interfaces           | Host filesystem mounts and /dev access shall be minimised. The container shall not receive unnecessary host privileges.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| CONT-07 | Platform Integrity              | Container images shall be authenticated and integrity-verified before deployment. Runtime configuration shall be protected against unauthorised modification.                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| CONT-08 | Network Protection              | Container networking shall permit only explicitly required connections. Unrestricted Internet connectivity shall be prevented.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| CONT-09 | WSCA Data Protection            | Volumes containing WSCA data shall be accessible only to authorised containers and processes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| CONT-10 | Privilege Escalation Protection | Privileged containers shall not be used. CAP_SYS_ADMIN and other unnecessary capabilities shall be removed. Seccomp and SELinux/AppArmor shall be applied where appropriate.                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| CONT-11 | Security-Relevant Logging       | Container runtime and security events shall be logged and made available to the platform monitoring infrastructure.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| CONT-12 | Vulnerability Management        | Container images, runtime components, Linux kernel components and dependencies shall be subject to vulnerability management.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| CONT-13 | Cyber Security Monitoring       | The container runtime and isolation mechanisms shall be monitored for security-relevant anomalies, including unauthorised container creation or modification, attempted isolation-boundary violations, unexpected resource access and suspicious workload behaviour. Detected events shall be forwarded to platform monitoring mechanisms for analysis, alerting and incident response. |

### 6.8 WSCA Execution Environment for Linux {#s-6-8}

The WSCA execution environment can combine the Linux mechanisms described above into a dedicated security boundary around the WSCA. The principal mechanisms are dedicated Linux user/group identities, filesystem permissions, SELinux/AppArmor, Linux capabilities, seccomp, systemd sandboxing, namespaces, cgroups, firewall controls, ASLR/NX and integrity protection of the WSCA executable and libraries.

This layer should provide the closest and most direct protection of the WSCA. It is therefore particularly relevant when demonstrating that the underlying platform does not introduce an attack path that would undermine the WSCA's AVA\_VAN.5 assessment.

| ID      | Security Principle    | Requirement Implementation for Linux                                                                                                                  |
|---------|-----------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| WSCA-01 | Minimal Configuration | The WSCA execution environment shall contain only the libraries, runtime components, configuration and supporting functionality required by the WSCA. |
| WSCA-02 | Limited Execution               | The WSCA executable and libraries shall be integrity-protected and only authorised versions shall be executed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| WSCA-03 | Least Privilege                 | The WSCA shall run under a dedicated non-root Linux account with only the required capabilities.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| WSCA-04 | Process Isolation               | The WSCA shall be isolated from unrelated processes using SELinux/AppArmor, namespaces and/or systemd sandboxing as appropriate.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| WSCA-05 | Memory Protection               | ASLR and NX/XD shall be enabled. Linux process isolation shall prevent other processes from accessing WSCA memory.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| WSCA-06 | Controlled Interfaces           | The WSCA shall have access only to explicitly required files, devices, sockets and system calls. seccomp and SELinux/AppArmor shall be used where appropriate to enforce this restriction.                                                                                                                                                                       |
| WSCA-07 | Platform Integrity              | The WSCA executable, libraries and security configuration shall be protected against unauthorised modification.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| WSCA-08 | Network Protection              | The WSCA shall communicate only with authorised endpoints. Linux firewall rules shall prevent unintended network connections.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| WSCA-09 | WSCA Data Protection            | WSCA credentials, cryptographic material and security-relevant configuration shall be protected using restrictive filesystem permissions and mandatory access controls.                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| WSCA-10 | Privilege Escalation Protection | The WSCA shall execute with no unnecessary capabilities and shall use NoNewPrivileges, seccomp and mandatory access control where appropriate.                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| WSCA-11 | Security-Relevant Logging       | Security-relevant events affecting the WSCA execution environment shall be recorded and protected against unauthorised alteration.                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| WSCA-12 | Vulnerability Management        | All WSCA runtime libraries and platform dependencies shall be included in the vulnerability-management process.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| WSCA-13 | Cyber Security Monitoring       | The WSCA execution environment shall be monitored for security-relevant anomalies, including unauthorised changes to runtime components or configuration, unexpected WSCA behaviour, suspicious resource access and indicators of compromise. Detected events shall be forwarded to platform monitoring mechanisms for analysis, alerting and incident response. |
